keyframe_review.note: 1700-1756: 85,545 km2 (287 cells). Whole row (287 cells in 1700): the Mekong delta and the Đồng Nai, Bình Dương, Bà Rịa and Tây Ninh lowlands (179 cells, 132 of them in the Mekong Delta region), Bình Thuận (27 cells) and Ninh Thuận (1), which are Panduranga, and the Lâm Đồng (33), Đắk Nông (20) and Bình Phước (24) uplands with 3 Đắk Lắk cells (80 upland cells). The Post-Angkor page: 'Cambodia gradually lost control of the Mekong Delta' and 'by the end of the 17th century, the region was under full Vietnamese administrative control' (it names only the Mekong Delta); the Nguyễn lords page has the Vietnamese 'secured their hold on the rich Mekong Delta' after Cambodian raids (1739) and a Gulf of Siam port secured in 1755; the Mạc Cửu page has 'Hà Tiên was a part of Cambodia until the year 1714'. Not a Cambodian state in these years: the delta lowlands are drawn as nguyen-lords land (its ledger 1700 and 1755), Bình Thuận and Ninh Thuận belong to champa (Panduranga) and the uplands to nobody, since no page opened names them. Verdict wrong, not adjust, because the row holds no land of the Cambodian kingdom (capital Oudong, post-angkor-cambodia); whether the western delta stayed Cambodian to the cessions of 1732-1757 is not on any page opened (Mạc Cửu: only Hà Tiên, to 1714).

correction.text: empty: Vietnamese-ruled delta; nguyen-lords to 1777, then the Tây Sơn and Nguyễn Ánh in their own dossiers

keyframe_review.note: 1757-1799: 81,359 km2 (271 cells; the 17 western cells go to the Nguyễn outline), with the same Bình Thuận, Ninh Thuận and upland cells as the 1700 outline (108 of the 271). The Nguyễn lords hold the delta to 1777 ('By 1777, Gia Định was captured'); the Tây Sơn took Gia Định in 1776, Siam 'occupied part of the Mekong Delta' in 1785 (Tây Sơn page) and Nguyễn Ánh 'came back to Đại Việt' in 1788 and reclaimed most southern provinces (Nguyễn lords page, footnote). No page makes the delta Cambodian after 1700.

Infobox 'Gia Định (1775-1777, 1780-1783, 1788-1802)': the delta is Nguyễn Ánh's base, not Cambodian; Cliopatria's Nguyễn dynasty outline of 1803 holds 270 of these 271 cells (including Bình Thuận, which the Nguyễn dynasty took with Panduranga in 1832, not in 1803).

ledger.note: 1700: Cliopatria opens a separate 'Cambodia' row on the Mekong delta and the cells around it. Page silent on any new state: the Post-Angkor page, which Cliopatria cites as 'Cambodia Middle Period', describes one kingdom ('Cambodia (post-Angkor period)', capital Oudong 1620-1863). The row is the 295-cell land the Khmer Empire row loses in 1700 (287 of them here). This dossier is a null row: it holds no land, and the loss of the delta in 1700 is recorded once, in post-angkor-cambodia's ledger (and mirrored in nguyen-lords).

notes:
This is a Cliopatria row, not a state. The row 'Cambodia' (1700-1802, Wikidata Q424, Wikipedia 'Cambodia Middle Period') is the 295-cell land that the Khmer Empire row loses in 1700 (287 cells here): Whole row (287 cells in 1700): the Mekong delta and the Đồng Nai, Bình Dương, Bà Rịa and Tây Ninh lowlands (179 cells, 132 of them in the Mekong Delta region), Bình Thuận (27 cells) and Ninh Thuận (1), which are Panduranga, and the Lâm Đồng (33), Đắk Nông (20) and Bình Phước (24) uplands with 3 Đắk Lắk cells (80 upland cells). It shares no cell with the Nguyễn outline of 1700. 'Cambodia Middle Period' is the Post-Angkor period article, so the Cambodian kingdom of these years is the post-angkor-cambodia dossier (capital Oudong, written by another batch). This dossier therefore marks all three shapes wrong; it holds no land and has only the found and dissolve rows (the validator requires both), and no territorial events or wars.
Fix pass after review (2026-10-19): the first version carried a 1700 loss of 271 cells to nguyen-lords (a duplicate of post-angkor-cambodia's 1700 loss of the same land), a 1739-1749 contest and a 1755 loss of 17 cells (mirrors of nguyen-lords events, for land this dossier never holds) and a 1658-1755 war that started before the life. All four are removed. The mirrors belong in post-angkor-cambodia's ledger (the 1739-1749 contest on the Gulf of Siam coast and the 1755 loss of the western strip); nguyen-lords names post-angkor-cambodia for them. If the orchestrator would rather merge the Name 'Cambodia' into post-angkor-cambodia's cliopatria_names, this file can be dropped; whoever takes the row must leave Bình Thuận and Ninh Thuận to champa (Panduranga) and not draw the Lâm Đồng, Đắk Nông and Bình Phước uplands as Cambodian or Nguyễn without a page.
Open question (thin finding): did the delta west of Gia Định stay Cambodian until the Nguyễn cessions of 1732-1757? The Mạc Cửu page (third page opened, over the 1-2 budget at the reviewer's request) says only 'Hà Tiên was a part of Cambodia until the year 1714' (a footnote: he offered Hà Tiên to the Nguyễn that year); it is silent on Mỹ Tho, Vĩnh Long, Tầm Phong Long and the rest of the western delta, and the Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh page (read for nguyen-lords) has his expeditions 'placed the region firmly under Vietnamese administrative control' (undated). Left as the Post-Angkor page has it: the delta lowlands Nguyễn from 1700, the 17 western cells from 1755. kingdom-of-cambodia (1956-2024, also Q424) is a different, modern state and is not merged here.
Not on the pages: 1698 Gia Định is on the Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh page (see nguyen-lords); 1708 Hà Tiên as a transfer, 1714 (as a Nguyễn dependency), 1731-33 and 1757 Tầm Phong Long (the Post-Angkor and Mạc Cửu pages lack them), the Siamese occupation of part of the delta in 1785 (Tây Sơn page, no land). Page budget 3 of 2 (the third was the reviewer's suggestion).
